capital_structure_summary.ebitda_basis: Fitch-derived 2025 EBITDA of c.EUR 108m (analyst calculation: 2025 sales EUR 493m x Fitch-adjusted EBITDA margin 22.0%, both per Fitch). Fitch does not state the EBITDA figure directly. This is well below company-reported FY2024 adj. EBITDA of EUR 128.6m; Fitch cites 'lower EBITDA' in 2025 alongside restructuring costs, and Fitch-adjusted figures also typically exclude company add-backs, so the two are not like-for-like. FY2025 company-reported EBITDA not available - further diligence required.
capital_structure_summary.leverage: Fitch EBITDA leverage 8.5x at end-2025 (forecast 8.0x 2026, c.7.7x 2027). Analyst calculation 8.7x gross / 8.4x net on the derived EBITDA.
capital_structure_summary.maturity_wall: EUR 965m of senior secured commitments (EUR 125m RCF + EUR 840m TLB) mature between Dec-2027 and Jul-2028, 15-21 months from 27-Sep-2026. RCF becomes current in Dec-2026. No refinancing has completed as of 27-Sep-2026. Fitch's rating and Stable Outlook assume refinancing 'within the next six months' of 06-Jul-2026, i.e. by c.early Jan-2027.
capital_structure_summary.covenant: TLBs covenant-lite. RCF springing net leverage covenant of 9.5x, live when 40% or more drawn (EUR 50m on EUR 125m). RCF was 71% drawn at end-2025, so the test should have been engaged. Indicative headroom (analyst calculation on Fitch-derived EBITDA, not covenant-definition EBITDA): net senior secured leverage c.8.4x vs 9.5x, i.e. EBITDA could fall c.11% before a breach. Covenant-definition EBITDA (likely including add-backs) would increase this headroom but is not available. Actual compliance certificate figures not available - further diligence required.
capital_structure_summary.recovery: Fitch recovery analysis: going-concern EBITDA c.EUR 95m x 5.5x distressed multiple = EV c.EUR 523m; less 10% administrative claims = c.EUR 470m; less EUR 11m super senior local facilities = c.EUR 459m available for EUR 965m of senior secured claims (TLB EUR 840m + RCF assumed fully drawn at EUR 125m), implying c.48% recovery (analyst calculation from Fitch parameters; Fitch publishes only the RR4 band, 31-50%). Compares with a TLB price of 93.18 on 25-Sep-2026.

liquidity.fitch_assessment: Liquidity 'limited' / 'Constrained Liquidity' key rating driver. FCF historically negative, 'particularly weak' in 2025 (lower EBITDA, higher capex, sizeable interest, material restructuring costs). Fitch expects FCF to remain slightly negative near term, then broadly neutral to slightly positive through 2029. Material underperformance, larger working capital swings or higher capex 'may result in a downgrade to the CCC category'.
liquidity.known_2026_cash_calls: Fitch rating case: restructuring costs c.EUR 10m in 2026 (c.EUR 5m a year in 2027-28); pension contributions EUR 11-12m a year; capex 5.3% of revenue (c.EUR 26m on 2025 sales, analyst calculation); no dividends to 2030.
liquidity.covenant_context: Springing 9.5x net leverage covenant engaged at 40% utilisation (EUR 50m on EUR 125m); utilisation was 71% (EUR 89m) at end-2025, so the test should have been live at end-2025 test dates. Repaying below EUR 50m would require c.EUR 39m, more than 3x Fitch's EUR 12m available cash at end-2025, so the covenant is likely to stay live until the RCF is refinanced (analyst inference, not confirmed). Indicative headroom c.11% EBITDA cushion on Fitch-derived figures; see capital_structure_summary.covenant.

group_structure: No 9fin org chart exists for Rodenstock. Simplified structure from Fitch (Jul-2026), 9fin articles and Moody's references: Apax Partners funds (c.73%), Mubadala Investment Company (c.24%) and founders/management (c.3%) at the Apr-2021 close (current stakes not confirmed) own the group via Iris HoldCo GmbH (the entity Moody's rated at the 2021 financing). Rodenstock Group GmbH is the Fitch-rated issuer (IDR B-, Stable, 06-Jul-2026). Rodenstock GmbH (Munich) is the operating company. The EUR 840m TLB (EUR 660m + EUR 150m tranches per 9fin) and EUR 125m RCF rank pari passu under a single SFA dated 12-Apr-2021, amended and restated 24-May-2022, secured on share pledges, bank accounts and intercompany receivables of material subsidiaries, with guarantees from group companies representing at least 80% of group EBITDA. EUR 11m local facilities rank ahead (super senior per Fitch). German pension obligations (EUR 230.9m at FY2020) are unsecured. The SFA borrower entity, the intermediate holdco chain between Iris HoldCo GmbH and Rodenstock Group GmbH, the full guarantor list and the restricted group perimeter are not available.

trading.trend_read: Price path in four phases: (1) 2021 to early 2022 at or above par; (2) 2022 sell-off to an all-time low of 83.14 (Jan-2023), then recovery to c.98 by early 2024; (3) two company-specific legs down, the Apr-2024 Moody's negative outlook (-4.3pts in two weeks) and the Apr-2025 Caa1 downgrade (-4.3pts in a week, extending to 88.35 by mid-May-2025), with a 5.6pt rebound after FY2024 results; (4) since mid-2025, a lower range of c.89-94 with a spike low of 86.64 in early Apr-2026 that has no identified company catalyst on file. Since Jun-2026 the loans have been flat at 92.4-93.7, with little reaction to the Fitch assignment (+1pt) or the Moody's withdrawal. At 93.18 the loans sit 2.3pts below the 21-Mar-2025 reference (95.48) are up 0.4pts year to date (92.80 at 31-Dec-2025), and are 6.5pts above the Apr-2026 low. Over the last three months the price has been stable, not softening. A price in the low 90s for a loan maturing in c.20 months signals the market is pricing some refinancing risk but not a distressed outcome.
